questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Syria?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Syria article.

questions.proof: Damascus is the capital and largest city.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Syria?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Syria on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Syria article.

questions.proof: It borders Turkey to the north and northwest, Iraq to the east and southeast, Jordan to the south, and Israel and Lebanon to the southwest.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Syria?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Before 20th century” part of the Syria article.

questions.proof: Most of the indigenous population converted to Islam and adopted the Arabic language.

questions.prompt: What money is used in Syria?

hints.nudge: Money names often come from a country’s own words. The other three are spent in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Ba'athist Syria” part of the Syria article.

questions.proof: The Syrian pound lost 80% of its value, and the economy became partly state-owned and partly a war economy.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “When it ended, _____ controlled Lebanon and Syria.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “ended”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Independent Syria” part of the Syria article.

questions.proof: France controlled Syria until 1946 when Syria became its own country.
